title: The Seven Heavens and the Merkavah
summary: The seven heavens and what each one holds: the storehouses of snow and hail, the souls of the tzaddikim, and the treasures of life and peace, with a warning for one who stops learning to chat. Then Nevuchadnetzar's boast, "I will ascend above the clouds," and the Gemara's answer of how far the heavens really reach, who may be taught maaseh merkavah, Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar, the child who understood chashmal, and why the Sages wanted to hide Sefer Yechezkel.
key_ideas: Every level of heaven has its own purpose, and the highest holds the souls of the tzaddikim.
Wanting is not enough; a person has to act.
The higher a person tries to raise himself in arrogance, the lower he falls.
The deepest secrets of Torah are given only to someone ready to hold them.
